rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rebukes them for neglecting their own practice of good; the fault is abandoning good, not instructing others while falling short themselves.
rows.anchor: والغرض أن الله تعالى ذمهم على هذا الصنيع ونبههم على خطئهم (4) في حق أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A learned person must command good and should practice it too, following Shuʿayb's refusal to act contrary to his instruction.
rows.anchor: كما قال شعيب، عليه السلام: {وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sounder position among early and later scholars is that both commanding right and practicing it are obligatory; neglecting one does not cancel the other.
rows.anchor: فكل من الأمر بالمعروف وفعله واجب، لا يسقط أحدهما بترك الآخر على أصح قولي العلماء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say sinners must not forbid others' sins; Ibn Kathir calls this weak and says this verse gives them no proof.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أن مرتكب المعاصي لا ينهى غيره عنها، وهذا ضعيف، وأضعف منه تمسكهم بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، مالك
rows.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr told Rabiʿa that if only faultless people could enjoin good, no one would do so; Malik agreed that no one is without fault.
rows.anchor: قال مالك عن ربيعة: سمعت سعيد بن جبير يقول له: لو كان المرء لا يأمر بالمعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing people are especially blameworthy when they knowingly leave obedience and commit sin; Ibn Kathir says this is why warnings about it occur in hadith.
rows.anchor: فإنه ليس من يعلم كمن لا يعلم؛ ولهذا جاءت الأحاديث في الوعيد على ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Jundub reports the Prophet comparing a learned person who teaches good without practicing it to a lamp that lights others while burning itself; Ibn Kathir calls this route strange.
rows.anchor: عن جندب بن (1) عبد الله، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "مثل العالم الذي يعلم الناس الخير ولا يعمل به

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's night-journey vision of people whose lips were cut with fiery shears, an image of those who instruct others in good but neglect themselves.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "مررت ليلة أسري بي

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Anas's night-journey report about preachers' lips being cut is transmitted again by ʿAbd b. Humayd and several Ibn Mardawayh and Yazid b. Harun routes through Hammad; Ibn Mardawayh also gives a Thumama route mentioning tongues.
rows.anchor: عن ثمامة، عن أنس، قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "مررت ليلة أسري بي على أناس

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Ibn Hibban, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmit through Malik b. Dinar, Thumama, and Anas a similar night-journey warning about preachers whose lips are cut.
rows.anchor: عن مالك بن دينار، عن ثمامة، عن أنس بن مالك، قال: لما عرج برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر بقوم تقرض شفاههم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Usama reports the Prophet's warning that a man who preached good and forbade wrong without following his own advice will be dragged into Hell and confronted by those he instructed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي وائل، قال: قيل لأسامة -وأنا رديفه-: ألا تكلم عثمان؟

rows.speaker: البخاري ومسلم
rows.claim: Bukhari and Muslim also transmit the Usama report about a preacher who commands good but does not practice it.
rows.anchor: ورواه البخاري ومسلم، من حديث سليمان بن مهران الأعمش، به نحوه

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying God will pardon the unlettered on Judgment Day more readily than scholars; Ibn Kathir cites this to stress that knowledge increases responsibility.
rows.anchor: عن أنس، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله يعافي الأميين يوم القيامة ما لا يعافي العلماء

rows.speaker: بعض الآثار
rows.claim: An unattributed report says the ignorant person is forgiven seventy times before the learned person is forgiven once, underscoring that the knowledgeable and unknowing are unequal.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في بعض الآثار: أنه يغفر للجاهل سبعين مرة حتى يغفر للعالم مرة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir links the distinction between knowledgeable and unknowing people to the Qur'anic question whether those who know equal those who do not.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى: {قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب}

rows.speaker: الوليد بن عقبة
rows.claim: A report traced to the Prophet has people in Paradise ask people in Hell why they entered, since the saved learned from them; they answer that they preached but did not act. Ibn Asakir transmits it from al-Walid b. ʿUqba.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن عساكر في ترجمة الوليد بن عقبة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن أناسا من أهل الجنة يطلعون على أناس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas challenged a man who wanted to enjoin right to first examine three verses: this verse, the warning against saying what one does not do, and Shuʿayb's resolve to act consistently.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: إنه جاءه رجل، فقال: يا ابن عباس، إني أريد أن آمر بالمعروف

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports a Prophetic warning that one who calls people to a deed or saying without doing it remains under God's anger until he stops or practices it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من دعا الناس إلى قول أو عمل ولم يعمل هو به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the chain of the Ibn ʿUmar report about calling people to what one does not practice is weak.
rows.anchor: إسناده فيه ضعف، وقال إبراهيم النخعي

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi disliked preaching stories because of this verse, the warning against saying what one does not do, and Shuʿayb's refusal to contradict his teaching.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي: إني لأكره القصص لثلاث آيات

rows.speaker: مسلم بن عمرو
rows.claim: Muslim b. ʿAmr's poem mocks a preacher who renounces worldly pleasures for others while seeking support and comfort for himself.
rows.anchor:
وما أحسن ما قال مسلم بن عمرو:
ما أقبح التزهيد من واعظ … يزهد الناس ولا يزهد

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان الحيري
rows.claim: Abu ʿUthman al-Hiri likens an ungodly preacher urging piety to a physician who treats others while sick himself; the listeners wept.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: جلس أبو عثمان الحيري الزاهد يوما على مجلس التذكير فأطال السكوت

rows.speaker: أبو العتاهية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAtahiya says the preacher describes piety as though possessing it, while the scent of his sins exposes him.
rows.anchor:
وقال أبو العتاهية الشاعر:
وصفت التقى حتى كأنك ذو تقى

rows.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي
rows.claim: Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali says not to forbid a trait one practices; reform yourself first, then advice can be believed, followed, and useful.
rows.anchor:
وقال أبو الأسود الدؤلي:
لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله

rows.speaker: عبد الواحد بن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Asakir recounts ʿAbd al-Wahid b. Zayd's dream-directed visit to Maimuna al-Sawda, whom he found praying among sheep and wolves that neither fled nor attacked.
rows.anchor: وذكر الحافظ ابن عساكر في ترجمة عبد الواحد بن زيد البصري العابد الواعظ قال: دعوت الله أن يريني رفيقي في الجنة

rows.speaker: ميمونة السوداء
rows.claim: Maimuna says her reconciliation with God brought reconciliation between wolves and sheep; she warns Ibn Zayd to inspect his limbs and says worldly gifts sought through repentance can replace intimacy with estrangement.
rows.anchor: يقال لها: ميمونة السوداء، فقصدت الكوفة لأراها

rows.speaker: ميمونة السوداء
rows.claim: Maimuna's poem rebukes a preacher who scolds people for sins while himself remaining spiritually sick; if he had repented first, his words would find a truthful place in hearts.
rows.anchor: فقلت لها: عظيني. فقالت: يا عجبا من واعظ يوعظ، ثم قالت: يا ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ميمونة السوداء
rows.claim: Maimuna's continuing poem calls the preacher's own sinfulness a strange wrong and says his admonition would gain credibility if he first corrected or repented of his own misguidance.
rows.anchor: يا واعظا قام لا حساب … يزجر قوما عن الذنوب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid identify the preventers as Christians, who threw filth into Jerusalem's Temple and stopped people praying there.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه} قال: هم النصارى. وقال مجاهد: هم النصارى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Nebuchadnezzar and his followers destroyed Jerusalem's Temple with Christian assistance.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وسعى في خرابها} هو بختنصر وأصحابه، خرب بيت المقدس، وأعانه على ذلك النصارى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: In another report, Qatada calls the Christians God's enemies and says hatred of the Jews drove them to help the Babylonian Magian Nebuchadnezzar destroy Jerusalem's Temple.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد، عن قتادة: قال: أولئك أعداء الله النصارى، حملهم بغض اليهود

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Christians backed Nebuchadnezzar's destruction and disposal of corpses in the Temple; the Romans helped because Israel had killed John son of Zechariah, a report also attributed to al-Hasan al-Basri.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: كانوا ظاهروا بختنصر على خراب بيت المقدس حتى خربه، وأمر به أن تطرح فيه الجيف

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the preventers as the Meccan polytheists who barred the Prophet at Hudaybiya, forcing him to sacrifice at Dhu Tuwa and make a truce; they objected that he had killed their fathers at Badr.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها}

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd explains striving to ruin the mosques as cutting off those who maintain them through remembrance and come for pilgrimage or ʿumra.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: {وسعى في خرابها} قال: إذ قطعوا من يعمرها بذكره ويأتيها للحج والعمرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas says Quraysh prevented the Prophet from praying at the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque, and the verse was revealed about that.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن قريشا منعوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة عند الكعبة في المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers the Christian account, arguing that Quraysh did not seek to ruin the Kaaba whereas the Romans did seek to ruin Jerusalem's Temple.
rows.anchor: ثم اختار ابن جرير القول الأول، واحتج بأن قريشا لم تسع في خراب الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers Ibn Zayd's Meccan-polytheist interpretation, also reported from Ibn ʿAbbas; Christians barring Jewish prayer would imply their religion was more upright, although Jewish remembrance then was rejected after their curse.
rows.anchor: قلت: الذي (1) يظهر -والله أعلم-القول الثاني، كما قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence moves from rebuking Jews and Christians to the polytheists who expelled the Prophet and his companions and barred them from prayer at the Sacred Mosque; Ibn Kathir cites 8:34, 9:17–18, and 48:25.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فإنه تعالى لما وجه الذم في حق اليهود والنصارى، شرع في ذم المشركين الذين أخرجوا الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir counters that Quraysh did ruin the Kaaba in substance by expelling the believers and occupying it with idols, partners, and polytheism.
rows.anchor: وأما اعتماده على أن قريشا لم تسع في خراب الكعبة، فأي خراب أعظم مما فعلوا؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maintaining mosques means remembering God, establishing His law, and cleansing them of impurity and idolatry, not merely decorating or constructing them.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد من عمارتها زخرفتها وإقامة صورتها فقط، إنما عمارتها بذكر الله فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is a declarative form carrying a command: when able, Muslims should permit such people to enter mosques only under truce and payment of jizya.
rows.anchor: هذا خبر معناه الطلب، أي لا تمكنوا هؤلاء -إذا قدرتم عليهم-من دخولها إلا تحت الهدنة والجزية

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: After the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet ordered a proclamation at Mina in year nine: no polytheist would make pilgrimage or perform naked circumambulation after that year, while existing covenants ran to term; Ibn Kathir links this to 9:28.
rows.anchor: ولهذا لما فتح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مكة أمر من العام القابل في سنة تسع أن ينادى برحاب منى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they should enter only trembling and apprehensive that believers might strike them, rather than seize the mosques and bar believers; that was the rightful order absent unbelievers' injustice.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: ما كان ينبغي لهم أن يدخلوا مساجد الله إلا خائفين على حال التهيب، وارتعاد الفرائص من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also foretells Muslim victory over the Sacred Mosque and other mosques, with polytheists entering the Haram only in fear; God fulfilled this by barring them and removing other religions from Arabia to purify the blessed place of the universal Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن هذا بشارة من الله للمسلمين أنه سيظهرهم على المسجد الحرام وعلى سائر المساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly humiliation repays their conduct: because they barred believers from the Sacred Mosque, they were barred from it and expelled from Mecca as they had expelled the believers.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الخزي لهم في الدنيا؛ لأن الجزاء من جنس العمل. فكما صدوا المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their afterlife punishment answers their violation of the House's sanctity through setting up idols around it, invoking others there, naked circumambulation, and other condemned practices.
rows.anchor: من نصب الأصنام حوله، والدعاء إلى غير الله عنده والطواف به عريا

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar says Christians conquered and ruined Jerusalem's Temple, after which the verse was revealed; no Christian enters Jerusalem except fearfully.
rows.anchor: فقال كعب الأحبار: إن النصارى لما ظهروا على بيت المقدس خربوه (8) فلما بعث الله محمدا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says no Roman enters Jerusalem's Temple in his time without fearing beheading or being made afraid by paying jizya.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: فليس في الأرض رومي يدخله اليوم إلا وهو خائف أن يضرب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they enter the mosques furtively, as if stealing in.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: لا يدخلون المساجد إلا مسارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jerusalem account still fits the verse's general meaning: Christians desecrated the rock toward which Jews prayed and were humbled there, while the Jews' even greater disobedience brought a greater punishment.
rows.anchor: قلت: وهذا لا ينفي أن يكون داخلا في معنى عموم الآية فإن النصارى ما ظلموا بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: السدي، عكرمة، وائل بن داود
rows.claim: Al-Suddi, ʿIkrima, and Wa'il b. Dawud interpret worldly humiliation as the appearance of the Mahdi.
rows.anchor: وفسر هؤلاء الخزي من الدنيا، بخروج المهدي عند السدي، وعكرمة، ووائل بن داود

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets worldly humiliation as payment of jizya in submission.
rows.anchor: وفسره قتادة بأداء الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says worldly humiliation is broader than the cited interpretations and quotes a hasan Prophetic supplication seeking protection from worldly humiliation and afterlife punishment; the report is not in the Six Books and Busr b. Artat has only one other report noted here.
rows.anchor: وهذا حديث حسن، وليس في شيء من الكتب الستة، وليس لصحابيه وهو بسر (6) بن أرطاة -ويقال: ابن أبي أرطاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the qibla was the first Qur'anic abrogation: after migration, the Prophet faced Jerusalem for over a year at God's command, though he loved Abraham's qibla and prayed looking skyward; the change unsettled the Jews, and God had tested who followed the Messenger.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس: كان أول ما نسخ من القرآن القبلة

words: قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbas report says that after praying toward Jerusalem the Prophet raised his head to heaven; God revealed the change toward the Kaaba, with Gabriel directing him toward its water-spout.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سلم من صلاته إلى بيت المقدس رفع رأسه إلى السماء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Yahya b. Qumta saw ʿAbd Allah b. ʿAmr facing toward the Kaaba's mizab and explaining that the commanded direction was toward it; al-Hakim graded the chain sound and said the two compilers did not include it.
rows.anchor: قال: رأيت عبد الله بن عمرو (2) جالسا في المسجد الحرام، بإزاء الميزاب، فتلا هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: One of al-Shafiʿi's two positions requires facing the Kaaba itself, based on reports specifying its line or the direction of its mizab.
rows.anchor: وهكذا قال غيره، وهو أحد قولي الشافعي، رحمه الله: إن الغرض إصابة عين القبلة

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: The majority position, also attributed to al-Shafiʿi, requires facing the Kaaba's direction; Ali glosses shatr as its qibla, and al-Hakim grades the report sound.
rows.anchor: والقول الآخر وعليه الأكثرون: أن المراد المواجهة

rows.speaker: أبو العالية، مجاهد، عكرمة، سعيد بن جبير، قتادة، الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya, Mujahid, ʿIkrima, Saʿid b. Jubayr, Qatada, and al-Rabiʿ b. Anas support facing the Kaaba's direction; Ibn Kathir cites the rule that the area between east and west is qibla.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول أبي العالية، ومجاهد، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report quoted by al-Qurtubi from Ibn ʿAbbas says the qibla is between east and west for mosque-goers, the mosque for people of the Haram, and the Haram for people across the earth.
rows.anchor: وقال القرطبي: روى ابن جريج عن عطاء عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ما بين المشرق والمغرب قبلة لأهل المسجد

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Bara' reports the Prophet faced Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months; after the change during the afternoon prayer, a man informed another congregation, who turned toward the House while still bowing.
rows.anchor: عن البراء أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى قبل بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر شهرا،

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: A second route from al-Bara' says the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, wished to turn toward the Kaaba, and was redirected when this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرزاق: أخبرنا إسرائيل، عن أبي إسحاق، عن البراء

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid b. al-Muʿalla recounts hearing the Prophet read the verse from the minbar; before the Prophet led noon prayer, he and a companion hid to perform two cycles, becoming the first to pray toward the new qibla.
rows.anchor: وروى النسائي عن أبي سعيد بن المعلى قال: كنا نغدو إلى المسجد على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
